clue.text: Offer arm round for dance

parts.note: an arm is a limb of the body
a round shape is the letter O

explanation.surface: Someone offers a partner their arm before taking the floor for a dance.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Offer' and 'for' only join the pieces; the arm is held out so that a ring, O, can be added to it.
explanation.definitionFit: The limbo is a Caribbean dance in which performers lean back to pass under a lowered bar.

clue.text: The Bard's was lost: no reward for it

definitions.meaning: Shakespeare, the Bard, wrote the comedy Love's Labour's Lost, its title echoing this phrase
work done for the love of it, with no payment expected

explanation.surface: Shakespeare's effort went unrewarded.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase names unpaid work done for pleasure, and Shakespeare's comedy title turns its words around.

clue.text: Defeated in game, but given match

definitions.meaning: paired with a partner, as birds or animals are

explanation.surface: A chess player loses but is consoled with a partner.
explanation.definitionFit: In chess a king is mated when beaten; animals are mated when paired with a partner.

clue.text: Why peeps heard in kitchen? Bird could be

definitions.text: Why peeps heard in kitchen? Bird could be

parts.words: Why peeps heard in kitchen? Bird could be
parts.note: chicks peeping in a kitchen suggests a bird there, plucked and trussed for roasting, prepared and waiting for the cooker

explanation.surface: A puzzled cook hears cheeping in the kitchen and wonders why.
explanation.definitionFit: A supermarket chicken sold prepared for roasting, needing no further work, is labelled with this term.

clue.text: Wonderful girl in charge, a sweetly-decorative thing

parts.note: a lovely girl is called an angel

explanation.surface: A lovely young woman in charge of something pretty and sweet.
explanation.definitionFit: Candied stems of this herb are used as green decoration on cakes and trifles.

clue.text: Just like carrier to be in the wrong place

parts.note: as means just like, in comparisons
a tray is something used to carry things

explanation.surface: A carrier that is just like something else ends up misplaced.
explanation.definitionFit: Something gone astray has wandered off course and is lost or mislaid.

clue.text: Batsman's essentials may be locked in the car

definitions.text: Batsman's essentials may be locked in the car

parts.words: Batsman's essentials may be locked in the car
parts.note: a cricket batsman wears gloves and a protective box, and a car has a lockable compartment in its dashboard

explanation.surface: A cricketer's kit is left locked in a vehicle.
explanation.definitionFit: The small lockable compartment in a car's dashboard is named for the driving gloves once kept there.

clue.text: Town near Glyndebourne cycle west a bit

indicators.note: the letters needed are only a bit of the words cycle west, sitting within them

explanation.surface: A cyclist heads a little west to reach a town near the opera house.
explanation.walkthrough: Glyndebourne is a country-house opera festival in East Sussex.
explanation.definitionFit: Lewes is the county town of East Sussex, a few miles from Glyndebourne opera house.

clue.text: Putting in hours in the park at this?

definitions.text: Putting in hours in the park at this?

parts.words: Putting in hours in the park at this?
parts.note: putting on a lawn game laid out like a dial, with holes at the hour positions

explanation.surface: Someone spends hours in the park.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Putting' looks like the verb put, but it is the golf stroke; 'hours' are the twelve numbered positions round the circle.
explanation.definitionFit: It is a putting game played on a lawn with targets arranged in a circle like the numbers on a dial.

clue.text: In bad debt case, wrong and right reversed by court, relative to David

indicators.note: in says the following pieces go inside the jumbled letters
case says the jumbled letters enclose the rest
bad says the letters of debt are put into a poor order
reversed means the two words wrong and right are turned back to front together

parts.note: a tort is a civil wrong in law
yes is a word of agreement, meaning right
to court a sweetheart is to woo

explanation.surface: In a bad-debt case, a court overturns the verdict on wrong and right.
explanation.walkthrough: 'In' and 'case' both signal the container, 'bad' the anagram, and 'reversed' turns wrong and right together; 'by' is only a link. David is Dickens's David Copperfield.
explanation.definitionFit: In Dickens's David Copperfield, this formidable woman is David's great-aunt.

clue.text: Well-behaved, like our pre-WWI currency?

definitions.meaning: said of a child who behaves perfectly
before the First World War British money was backed by, and exchangeable for, gold

explanation.surface: A well-behaved child compared to old money.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom praises a child for good conduct; literally, money of the gold standard era was worth its gold.

clue.text: Commit to pass inside

definitions.meaning: to promise or take on a task
to overtake a vehicle on the nearside, the wrong side

explanation.surface: A driver resolves to overtake on the inside.
explanation.definitionFit: To promise to do something is one sense; British drivers also use it for overtaking on the wrong, inner side.

clue.text: Bill, the villain, I misplaced in the heavens

indicators.note: misplaced says the letter I is taken out of its spot and put elsewhere

parts.note: the heavens are the skies

explanation.surface: A villain named Bill loses his place in the heavens.
explanation.definitionFit: Bill Sikes is the brutal burglar in Dickens's Oliver Twist.

clue.text: Shabby cover for novel? No

definitions.meaning: a worn, outdated piece of headwear
the opposite of new: stale and unoriginal

explanation.surface: A tatty dust jacket rejected for a new book.
explanation.definitionFit: A worn hat is literally shabby headgear; figuratively the phrase means stale and far from new.

clue.text: Cut out round neck area? Not half!

definitions.text: Cut out round neck area? Not half!

parts.words: Cut out round neck area? Not half!
parts.note: a dress cut very low around the neck and shoulders; 'Not half!' is a British exclamation meaning 'and how!'

explanation.surface: A dressmaker cuts out a neckline, emphatically.
explanation.definitionFit: The French term describes a garment with a low neckline that bares the neck and shoulders.

clue.text: No way lover boy lacks energy in this book

parts.note: taken as written
ST is the abbreviation for street, a way

indicators.note: lacks says a letter is missing from the lover

parts.note: Romeo is the archetypal young lover
E is the symbol for energy in physics

explanation.surface: A book in which a would-be lover has no way forward and runs out of steam.
explanation.definitionFit: Nostromo is a 1904 novel by Joseph Conrad, so it is the book in question.

clue.text: Elephant perhaps a valuable advantage, with tree to be uprooted

parts.note: a trump is a card or resource giving a decisive edge

indicators.note: uprooted says the tree's letters are pulled out of place and scrambled

explanation.surface: An elephant uproots a tree, which gives it an advantage.
explanation.definitionFit: An elephant trumpets when it calls, so it is one example of something that trumpets.

clue.text: What's kept in reserve to make big winning margin

definitions.meaning: a reserved person keeps people at arm's length
in horse racing, a win by more than thirty lengths

explanation.surface: Holding something back to win by a large margin.
explanation.definitionFit: Keeping your distance means being reserved, and racing records a huge victory as a win by this.

clue.text: Duly pick at random here?

indicators.note: random says the letters of duly pick are put in no fixed order

explanation.surface: A fairground stall where you pick a prize blindly.
explanation.definitionFit: A tub of wrapped prizes at a fair, from which you draw one blindly, is a place to pick at random.

clue.text: Almost certain to be handed information, having used Internet

indicators.note: almost says the word for certain stops just short, losing its final letter

parts.note: sure means certain
to be fed information is to be supplied with it

explanation.surface: Someone almost certain to be given information.
explanation.definitionFit: To surf the Internet is to browse it, so surfed means having browsed online.

clue.text: Take up a profession — allow there should be money in it

definitions.text: there should be money in it

indicators.note: in a down clue, take up means the word is read upwards, backwards

parts.note: law is a profession
let means allow

explanation.surface: Someone takes up a profession hoping it pays.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Take up a profession' reads as choosing a career, but 'Take up' turns LAW backwards in this down entry.
explanation.definitionFit: A wallet is a pocket case meant to hold cash, so money should be in it.

clue.text: One on hand shortly to switch flow of water

indicators.note: in an across clue, on places one piece after the other
switch says the trimmed word is turned round
shortly says the word is cut short by its final letter

parts.note: a glove is what goes on a hand
A means one

explanation.surface: Someone wants a hand on deck to divert the flow of water.
explanation.walkthrough: 'shortly' drops the final letter, 'to switch' turns what remains round, and 'on' sets the A after it. 'One on hand' reads as a helper, but it is what a hand wears.
explanation.definitionFit: The Volga is Europe's longest river, a great flow of water through Russia.

clue.text: Confused, and of no fixed abode

definitions.meaning: bewildered, not knowing what to do
out on the ocean, with no fixed position on land

explanation.surface: A confused homeless person.
explanation.definitionFit: Sailors far from land are literally on the ocean; figuratively the idiom means bewildered.

clue.text: Big and powerful, head to foot — such signs of success

indicators.note: head to foot says the first letter goes to the end

parts.note: strapping means big and strong

explanation.surface: A strapping figure seen from head to foot looks successful.
explanation.definitionFit: Trappings are the outward show of status, such as cars and clothes, that signal success.

clue.text: Irritates, getting lifeboat on to bearing of 0 degrees?

indicators.note: on to says the boat is placed onto the line of bearing, sitting within it

parts.note: the north-south line, N and S, is the line of zero degrees on a compass
Noah's ark was a lifeboat that saved those aboard

explanation.surface: A lifeboat steering due north provokes irritation.
explanation.walkthrough: 'getting' is a link; 'bearing' is the compass, not tolerance.
explanation.definitionFit: To nark someone is British slang for annoying them.

clue.text: What singular loner operates, on the move?

definitions.text: What singular loner operates, on the move?

indicators.note: on the move says the letters are set moving into a new order

parts.note: S is the abbreviation for singular in grammar

explanation.surface: A loner operating something while walking about.
explanation.walkthrough: Mix S (singular) with LONER OPERATES; the whole clue also describes a portable cassette player used by one person while walking.
explanation.definitionFit: A portable cassette or CD player with headphones is used by one person, often walking along.

clue.text: Declining to give years to good books

parts.note: a decade is ten years
NT is the New Testament, books of the Good Book

explanation.surface: Someone declines to give years to studying the Bible.
explanation.definitionFit: A decadent society is one in moral or cultural decline.

clue.text: Brought up soundly, but destroyed

indicators.note: soundly says the word for brought up is heard, not spelt

parts.note: a child brought up is raised

explanation.surface: Someone brought up well, yet destroyed.
explanation.definitionFit: To rase a building is an old spelling of raze, to destroy it completely.
